ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. corporate regime); Decree 410 of 1971 (Código de Comercio); Law 526 of 1999 (creation of UIAF); Law 1129 of 2007 (AML/CFT organic statute); Law 2010 of 2019, Article 23 (final beneficiary definition and registration duty); DIAN Resolution 000100 of 2021 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); Superintendencia de Sociedades Circular 014 of 2020 (SARLAFT obligations for supervised entities); UIAF Circular 001 of 2021 (money laundering typologies and sectoral reporting thresholds).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal) of the foreign corporate shareholder, issued within 90 days before filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registrar or competent registry authority in the country of origin (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, or equivalent commercial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961; consular legalization if the country of origin is not a party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) granted by each foreign shareholder and UBO to the Colombian incorporator and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille after notarization, followed by sworn official translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or shareholders' resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Colombian S.A.S., the subscribed capital, and the appointment of the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or legal representative of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille after notarization of the corporate signatures; sworn Spanish translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all UBOs and the designated legal representative(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the country of origin or the corresponding embassy/consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certified copy before a Colombian notary; apostille not required when originals are exhibited in-country for certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal records certificate (Certificado de Antecedentes Penales / certificate of no criminal record) of the legal representative(s) and, where applicable, UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Policía Nacional de Colombia for residents; competent criminal records authority of the foreign jurisdiction for non-residents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct domestic issuance for Colombian residents; Hague Apostille for foreign certificates, with sworn Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, shareholders, and initial trade counterparties against the UIAF PEP database, the Colombian SARLAFT risk lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and the Colombian national criminal intelligence databases; enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP status, exposure to OECD high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions, or involvement of politically exposed intermediaries; SARLAFT records must be retained for 10 years and suspicious transaction reports (ROS) filed with UIAF under Section 53 of Law 1129 of 2007.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via the competent Cámara de Comercio in the chosen domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), with final company registration mirrored to the Superintendencia de Sociedades; online pre-clearance is processed through the chamber's 'homologación de nombre' service.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Spanish and may include foreign words only if written in the Latin alphabet and accepted as customary in Colombian commercial usage; the acronym 'S.A.S.' must be appended to the name; all registry filings must be in Spanish or accompanied by a sworn official translation by a Colombian traductor público oficial; names must be clearly distinguishable from existing registered names and must not produce misleading confusion with trademarks or regulated sectors.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANCO / FINANCIERA / FIDUCIARIA (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia)
SEGUROS / REASEGUROS / CORREDORA DE SEGUROS (regulated insurance sector)
COOPERATIVA / FONDO DE EMPLEADOS / PREVISORA (reserved to cooperative and mutual sector entities)
NACIONAL / GOBIERNO / MINISTERIO / PRESIDENCIA / DEPARTAMENTO ADMINISTRATIVO (state-affiliated terms requiring State authorization)
COLOMBIA (requires registered trademark rights with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio or authorization from the Ministry of Interior)
UNIVERSIDAD / COLEGIO / INSTITUTO EDUCATIVO (requires Ministry of Education approval)
INVIMA / MEDICAMENTOS / HOSPITAL / CLÍNICA (sanitary tokens requiring prior INVIMA or Ministry of Health authorization for food and health-related names)
ALCALDÍA / GOBERNACIÓN / POLICÍA / FUERZAS MILITARES (public authority denominations)
PETRÓLEOS / MINERÍA / ENERGÍA (hydrocarbon and mining terms subject to ministerial licensing constraints)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the Cámara de Comercio, the applicant may file a recurso de reposición before the same chamber within 10 business days of notification under CPACA (Law 1437 of 2011); if the chamber maintains the rejection, the applicant may file a recurso de apelación where the decision is appealable before the Superintendencia de Sociedades, and thereafter pursue judicial review before the Contentious Administrative Jurisdiction. An alternative name may be filed simultaneously in the same or another Chamber of Commerce to avoid delay; the UBO must also ensure that the rejected name does not conflict with a pending trademark registration before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted for ISIC 4633 dairy wholesaling. The S.A.S. must maintain a physical and verifiable registered office (domicilio social) in Colombia; a virtual or shared office address cannot serve as the statutory domicile for this regulated activity because INVIMA sanitary oversight, physical storage and inspection of raw milk powder imports, documentary retention, and fiscal domicile verification require an operational presence. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary administrative correspondence address, not as the registered principal place of business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated - estimated 45% annual likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspections by INVIMA (sanitary inspection of dairy storage and import operations), the Superintendencia de Sociedades (corporate substance and registry audits), and DIAN (tax domicile and invoicing verification); the probability increases if the registered address is flagged as a virtual office, if import volumes exceed sanitary thresholds, or if the company is selected for a SARLAFT/AML supervisory visit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Primary: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedades por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 17, 22, 40-45; Supplementary: Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), Articles 110, 353-356; Consolidated Regulatory Decree: Decreto 1074 de 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered seat (for Bogotá D.C.: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), operating through the national Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (Private Incorporation Instrument) filed for commercial registration; where contributions include real estate or in-kind assets above the statutory threshold, the instrument must be elevated to an Escritura Pública (Public Deed) executed before a Notario under Article 5 of Ley 1258 de 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-in capital is required for an S.A.S. under Ley 1258 de 2008; the founders may establish any capital from zero upward. Any subscribed capital must be fully paid within two (2) years from incorporation (Article 4). Payments may be made in cash, in-kind, or by capitalization of credits; no escrow or blocked-account mandate applies at the formation stage. The Chamber registration tax is calculated at 0.7% of declared capital for private instruments.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S.

At a meeting of the sole shareholder held in Bogotá D.C., Colombia, the following resolutions were adopted unanimously:

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The subscribed capital of COP [amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares, is approved and ratified.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The legal seat and principal place of business are fixed at [address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia.

3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [Shareholder 1] is appointed Legal Representative (Representante Legal), and [Shareholder 2] is appointed Secretary. Each appointee is authorized to execute the Chamber of Commerce registration, obtain the NIT/RUT before DIAN, open corporate bank accounts, and represent the company in all incorporation proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Validation of the Corporate Name (Homonimia Certification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — RUES virtual consultation portal (www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the name-validation request in the RUES portal for the proposed corporate name and at least one alternative; the Chamber issues the Certificado de Homonimia confirming that no identical active name is registered in the national commercial registry. The certificate remains valid for 30 calendar days for use in the incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Identification document of the founding shareholder or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for homonymy or identity with a registered trademark, file an alternative validated name; an opposition or corrective application can be filed before the same Chamber within five (5) business days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Instrument (Documento Privado de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders directly; a Notaría (Public Notary) is added where the statutory in-kind or real-estate contribution threshold requires public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the full constitutive document containing the corporation name, corporate purpose (cross-border wholesale trading of whole and skimmed milk powder), capital distribution, representation, audit and governance provisions; execute signatures of all founding shareholders; have signatures certified by a notary when the document is presented to the Chamber for registration.
required_dossiers: Valid national or foreign identification (cédula de ciudadanía or passport)
Certification of no prior tax or commercial obligations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or a shareholder detects defective clauses, re-execute the instrument with corrected language; non-essential invalid clauses are severable and do not invalidate the creation of the company (Article 5, Ley 1258 de 2008).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Public Commercial Registry and Issuance of the Matrícula Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá — Registro Público Mercantil window / RUES electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation instrument together with the Formulario Único de Registro Empresarial (FUR), the RUT entry form, and the proof of payment of the inscription rights and registration tax. The Chamber verifies the filing and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, conferring legal personality and registering the mercantile establishment as of the filing date.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución (or Escritura Pública)
Receipt of the registration fee and tax payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a query (requerimiento), correct or supplement the documentation within the granted term (normally 10-20 business days) through the SEDE virtual platform; failure to cure within the term causes the filing to be deemed not completed, requiring a fresh submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Customs Registration with DIAN (NIT and RUT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) — virtual RUT registration office (www.dian.gov.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, complete the binding RUT registration to obtain the NIT; select the applicable tax statuses (IVA responsible, withholding agent, national consumption regime), activate the electronic invoicing system, and file the export-import customs registration data within the RUT electronic form.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Identification document of the legal representative
Address verification of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or queries the RUT, correct the data in the virtual portal within the response term and re-submit; if the NIT is already assigned to another entity, request the cancellation and re-issuance through the DIAN customer-service channel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – national tax and customs authority; digital clearance portals: www.dian.gov.co and the MUISCA transactional system (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) for RUT, NIT, electronic invoicing and export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident establishing a Colombian S.A.S.: (1) incorporate via private document filed with the Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce), with notarized legalization and foreign-investment registration (Registro de Inversión Extranjera with Banco de la República) when equity is contributed in foreign currency; (2) obtain the chamber certificate (certificado de existencia y representación legal) appointing the legal representative; (3) apply to DIAN through MUISCA or a DIAN office for RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), which is typically assigned automatically upon incorporation; (4) update the RUT to reflect the status of 'Responsable de IVA' and the economic activity code 4633 (wholesale of dairy products), plus exporter status (exportador); (5) register in DIAN customs' exporter systems and obtain any required sanitary authorization (INVIMA free-sale certificate) for dairy powder exports; and (6) register as an employer for payroll/social security if local staff are hired. Registration must be completed before the first taxable transaction or import.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Colombian S.A.S. is a tax-resident juridical person subject to entity-level corporate income tax (35% for tax year 2025) on worldwide income; it is not eligible for pass-through treatment and no tax-consolidation regime applies. Foreign-source income is generally taxable with a foreign tax credit (Article 254 ET); the territorial dividend exemption may apply only to qualifying equity participations in foreign companies. The S.A.S. is also subject to dividend withholding tax (10% plus the 7.5% surtax under Law 2277/2022 where applicable) on distributions to non-resident shareholders. The entity files Form 110 (income tax) and Form 300/350 (IVA). No tax-exempt zone applies to the standard commercial export activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no US-style check-the-box pass-through election for corporations. Available statutory elections affecting the dairy export trade include: (1) election to claim refundable VAT 'saldos a favor' for exporters (Articles 481, 855 ET) via periodic bimonthly refund filings instead of offsetting future tax liabilities; (2) election to treat dividends and capital gains from non-resident entities as exempt under the territorial-divident regime (Article 49 ET) if the 20% minimum holding period and substance conditions are met; (3) election to enter into advance pricing agreements (APA) with DIAN to fix transfer-pricing margins for commodity sales to related parties; (4) election between general and accelerated depreciation for fixed assets; (5) exclusion from the simplified 'no responsable' VAT regime, which is reserved exclusively for individual small merchants and is not available to S.A.S. companies; and (6) optional application of the special VAT treatment for certain agricultural inputs where the dairy commodity qualifies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre las Ventas (VAT/GST), regulated by Articles 420 et seq. of the Estatuto Tributario (Colombian Tax Code).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold applies to corporations: every S.A.S. performing a taxable activity in Colombia must register for IVA in the RUT before the first transaction or import, regardless of revenue. The only low-turnover simplification (gross income below approximately COP 174,296,500, equal to 3,500 UVT for 2025) is restricted to individual merchants under the 'no responsables de IVA' regime and is unavailable to S.A.S. entities, importers or exporters of dairy goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing – 'factura electrónica de venta' (FEV) – applies to all DIAN-registered taxpayers including S.A.S. exporters. Each invoice must be generated as a signed XML, transmitted in real time to the MUISCA electronic-invoicing platform (either directly through the DIAN portal or via an authorized technology provider – proveedor tecnológico), pre-validated before completion of the transaction, and stamped with the CUNE (Código Único de Numeración Electrónica) or CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica). Colombia does not use physical fiscal stamps; the DIAN's digital transaction record serves as the fiscal control instrument. Export invoices must identify the 'exportación' modality, link to the corresponding customs export declaration (DEX), and be transmitted simultaneously with the dispatch. No cash-register ticket alone may evidence an export sale.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of whole and skimmed milk powder are 'excluidas' (excluded, with entitlement to input-VAT recovery) from IVA under Article 481 ET. Eligibility conditions: (1) the goods must physically depart Colombian customs territory under a valid Declaración de Exportación (DEX) accepted by DIAN; (2) the seller must be an IVA-responsible S.A.S. exporter; (3) title and risk must pass to a foreign buyer situated outside Colombia; (4) the FOB export value must be reported as an excluded sale in the periodic IVA return; (5) the net input-VAT balance ('saldo a favor') must be claimed through the formal refund mechanism (Form 110, Article 855 ET) within the statutory limits; and (6) export proceeds must be channelled through the Colombian foreign-exchange market (mercado cambiario) through an authorized intermediary bank. For dairy products, compliance with INVIMA export sanitary requirements is a precondition to customs clearance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (DEX) – export customs declaration accepted, validated and ratified by DIAN
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Colombian customs territory
Commercial invoice issued as an electronic invoice bearing CUNE/CUFE with the 'exportación' modality reference
Packing list, weight certificate and certificate of origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
Inward Remittance Certificate evidenced by the Declaración de Cambio (foreign-exchange conversion declaration) filed through the authorized Colombian intermediary bank
Visto bueno de embarque or terminal/port documentation supporting the export movement
INVIMA export sanitary certificate or free-sale certificate for dairy food products
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN's automated risk engine flags exporters for verification of DEX validation, foreign-buyer identity, e-invoice CUNE integrity, port and customs-movement traces, and foreign-exchange repatriation. Penalties: (1) inaccurate-return penalty ('sanción por inexactitud', Article 647 ET) of up to 100% of the tax difference attributable to erroneous zero-rating; (2) improper-refund penalty ('devoluciones improcedentes', Article 670 ET) of 10% on the claimed refund, plus interest ('intereses moratorios') at the effective bank lending rate; (3) mandatory clawback of the refunded amount, with DIAN authority to reassess the VAT position for up to four fiscal years (five where returns were not filed); (4) criminal liability for falsified export documentation or over-invoicing designed to fabricate refunds (Articles 402 and 434 of the Criminal Code; Law 1762 of 2015 anti-smuggling regime), carrying imprisonment and fines; (5) for failure to channel export proceeds within 180 days, forced channeling and administrative fines under the Banco de la República foreign-exchange regulations (Circular DCIN-83); and (6) administrative consequences including suspension or cancellation of the exporter and IVA-responsible status in the RUT and inclusion in DIAN's public risk lists.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia. Foreign exchange policy is implemented via the Junta Directiva del Banco de la República under External Resolution No. 1 of 2018 and Decree 1735 of 1993.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is convertible for current-account transactions (trade, services, remittances) and for registered capital transactions. Profit remittances from foreign direct investment are freely payable through the official foreign exchange market once the FDI is registered with Banco de la República. No prior license is required for trade-related FX, but all transactions must be carried out through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries or bank accounts in Colombia. Capital-account operations (loans, injections, investment liquidation) require filing Form No. 4 and are subject to documentary verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from outward shipments of goods must be repatriated through authorized foreign exchange market intermediaries within six months of the date of shipment/customs declaration (or the payment term reflected in the commercial invoice, not exceeding the mandatory legal term). 100% of export proceeds must be sold in the official exchange market, or deposited in a foreign-currency deposit account held with a local authorized bank, unless a specific exemption applies under Resolution No. 1.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account (COP) and Foreign Currency Deposit Account (USD)
Operational Treasury Account (COP) and Foreign Currency Deposit Account (USD)
Operational Treasury Account (COP) and Foreign Currency Deposit Account (USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low. Offshore digital EMIs cannot legally open COP-denominated local accounts or independently access the Colombian official FX market. Colombian regulations (Ley 1735/2014) allow only supervised banking institutions and licensed payment providers to provide local accounts; cross-border EMIs can only partner with a local bank as a proxy, which adds operational risk and AML overhead without neutralizing FX formality.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the SAS legal representative (natural person) is generally mandatory at the selected bank's branches in Bogotá or Medellín during initial onboarding. Some banks provide remote onboarding if the UBO already maintains an individual relationship with the bank, but the local corporate officer must still appear for a manual signature verification. Bank certifications, chamber of commerce certificate, and notarized minutes are required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner appears in international sanctions lists or adverse media database
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented sanctions screening analysis from a recognized compliance tool; independent legal opinion on the UBO's record; fully sourced ownership/control chart; contracts and invoices evidencing commercial legitimacy of the dairy trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected monthly trade volumes inconsistent with declared paid-in capital or office premises
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sales/purchase agreements for milk powder, customs broker engagement letter, warehouse/receiving terminal evidence, and board resolution approving treasury limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FX transactions with counterparties located in high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Venezuela, certain offshore financial centers)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Know-your-supplier reports, documented trade procedures under Incoterms, proof of title transfer (warehouse warrants/bills of lading), and record of underlying trade finance instrument (LC).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the Colombian SAS must be received via an authorized local bank using SWIFT wire instructions; the incoming remittance must include purpose code 'Direct investment in Colombia (Inversión Extranjera Directa)' and the beneficiary's NIT (tax ID). The investment must be registered with Banco de la República using Form No. 4 before the funds are disposed of, supported by the constitutive deed, UBO certificate, and bank certificate. The funds must remain in the operational account until the exchange transaction is recorded with the official intermediary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlements of milk powder imports/suppliers, all payments must be processed through a local bank via SWIFT MT103 or documentary credit chain. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) opened by the Colombian bank to the overseas beneficiary are the preferred rail; each payment must be tied to the import declaration and use central bank concept code '4530 - Importation of goods' (or applicable code) filed with the foreign exchange form. Direct telegraphic transfers (TT) for amounts under USD 20,000 may be cleared without documentary LC but must still be filed in the FX system with appropriate invoice evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards on COP/USD with Banco de la República registered dealers (cash-settled or deliverable)
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on COP/USD traded with authorized local banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (COP vs USD) used to hedge balance-sheet exposure from trade debt

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal (renovación de la matrícula mercantil), with sliding Chamber tariff based on declared assets and liabilities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually due by 31 March after each 31 December fiscal year-end; not determined by incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a 10% late-payment surcharge on the tariff plus monthly interest; failure to renew for two consecutive years is a legal cause of dissolution and administrative strike-off by the Chamber; good-standing certificates are suspended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements, management report, and statutory auditor's opinion, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio; Superintendencia de Sociedades if under its permanent supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by 31 March for a calendar-year S.A.S.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and penalties imposed by the Cámara or Superintendencia, suspension of mercantile certificates, and possible forced liquidation for persistent failure to deposit statutory accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual shareholders' meeting minutes covering financial statements and profit distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate statutory books; no external filing, but the acta supports the financial-statement deposit with the Cámara
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held within three months of fiscal year-end, by 31 March for a calendar-year S.A.S.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unapproved financial statements bar lawful dividend distributions; administrators may incur joint liability; inaccurate minutes carry legal and criminal document penalties; no automatic Chamber strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner report (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales, RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May, or such date as published in DIAN's annual tax calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely, inaccurate, or incomplete filing may result in fines up to 15,000 SMMLV or 1% of gross income / 0.5% of assets as applicable; DIAN may suspend tax-related privileges, but no direct administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (declaración de renta y complementario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the DIAN filing window, generally from 3 March through 9 May following the tax year, assigned by the last two digits of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge from 3% to 10% of tax payable plus monthly default interest; accuracy penalties up to 200% of omitted amounts; persistent non-filing can suspend fiscal credentials and create administrator liability but does not itself trigger Chamber administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory when, as of the prior year-end: gross assets exceed 30,000 SMMLV, gross revenues exceed 30,000 SMMLV, or headcount exceeds 200 employees; it is also mandatory for companies designated Gran Contribuyente by DIAN or subject to permanent regulatory supervision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NIIF/IFRS as adopted in Colombia through Law 1314 of 2009 and Decree Único Reglamentario 2420 of 2015; a wholesale milk-powder trading S.A.S. normally applies NIIF para las PYMES (IFRS for SMEs, Group 2), with full IFRS (Group 1) only if it meets size, public-interest, or large-taxpayer thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Colombian S.A.S. must file the annual RUB with DIAN and identify all natural persons who directly or indirectly hold at least 5% of shares, voting rights, or interests, or who exercise control or receive economic benefit. Share transfers are recorded in the company's register of shareholders; the resulting ownership chain is reported in the next annual RUB. No separate UBO filing is submitted to the Cámara de Comercio.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Libro de Registro de Accionistas
Minute Book of the Shareholders' Assembly / Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas
Minute Book of the Board of Directors / Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva, if a board is appointed
Accounting books: journal, inventory, and balance-sheet ledgers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% for tax year 2024 (Articles 240 and 240-1, Colombian Tax Statute E.T.), applicable to all Colombian resident legal entities including an S.A.S. engaged in wholesale dairy trading.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to wholesale raw-milk-powder trading under ISIC 4633. The effective rate approximates the headline 35% after standard deductions for cost of goods sold, freight, customs duties, logistics and financing costs. The presumptive income (renta presuntiva) rate is suspended at 0% for tax year 2024. Interest paid to non-resident related lenders is deductible subject to the 3:1 thin-capitalization limitation of Article 118-1 E.T.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Sociedades Nacionales y Asimiladas) filed electronically through the DIAN MUISCA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return is due within the national DIAN filing calendar for the relevant tax year, generally running from 12 September through 17 October of the year following the fiscal year-end; the exact date is assigned by the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT. For fiscal years not ending on 31 December, the same national window applies after the close of the chosen fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All operating and non-operating revenue from wholesale raw milk powder, whole milk powder and skimmed milk powder trade (ISIC 4633 / NAICS 424430), reported on an accrual basis, including export sales, domestic resale, commissions and financial income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian S.A.S. must report its worldwide income as a resident entity. A foreign seller of dairy goods without a Colombian permanent establishment does not derive Colombian-source income under Article 24 E.T. and is not required to file Form 210.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of merchandise sold, ocean/air freight, insurance, customs duties, warehousing, demurrage, quality-control testing, and trade-finance charges directly related to the milk-powder commodity cycle.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All deductions must be supported by export/import declarations, bills of lading, warehouse receipts and valid electronic invoices satisfying Article 771-2 E.T. Cross-border purchases from related parties require arm's length pricing documentation under Article 260-1 E.T.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 36 - Net Taxable Income (Renta Líquida Gravable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after deducting costs, commercial expenses, exempt income (in accordance with the Article 254 imputation mechanism) and tax-loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward for 12 fiscal years; losses sourced from foreign branches or from activities outside the Colombian commercial scope cannot be offset against Colombian trading profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The 35% statutory corporate income tax rate is applied to net taxable income; no surcharge applies to commercial trading entities (the 5% financial-sector surcharge does not apply).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned S.A.S. entities receive no preferential rate. Dividends paid out of this 35%-taxed base become subject to an additional 5% shareholder-level withholding upon repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 57-58 - Net Tax Payable (Impuesto Neto y Valores a Pagar)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax reduced by withholdings already applied to income at source (retenciones en la fuente), advance payments (anticipos) and any available tax credits; resulting balance paid electronically through MUISCA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders may not credit their home-country taxes or the Colombian corporate tax against the additional 5% dividend surcharge; the obligation to pay the dividend withholding arises at the time of distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers Article 641 E.T.: 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of a month, up to a maximum of 100% of the tax; where no tax is due, a floor penalty of 10 UVT or 0.5% of gross income applies. Late payment accrues monthly default interest (interés moratorio) at the certified current banking rate. Filing an inaccurate return triggers Article 647 E.T.: a penalty equal to 100% of the omitted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends distributed by a Colombian S.A.S. to a non-resident shareholder are split: (i) the portion attributable to profits already subject to 35% corporate income tax bears a 5% additional withholding tax (Article 245 E.T.); (ii) the portion attributable to untaxed or exempt profits bears a 35% withholding tax (Article 246 E.T.). For a company distributing fully taxed profits, the effective additional repatriation charge is 5%; the combined corporate-plus-withholding burden on a distribution of untaxed profits can reach 57.75%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To access a reduced dividend rate under an applicable double taxation agreement (e.g., Canada, Spain, UK, Switzerland, Mexico, Chile, South Korea, Japan, India, France, Portugal, Czech Republic), the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the competent authority of the residence state for the calendar year of payment; (2) deliver to the Colombian paying S.A.S. the TRC, a sworn beneficial-ownership statement, and the legalized copy of the DTA; (3) instruct the payer to apply the treaty rate at source. If the statutory rate was already withheld, the shareholder must file a refund claim before the DIAN (solicitud de devolución y/o compensación) with supporting documentation, generally within the 5-year statute of limitations; administrative processing routinely exceeds 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest paid to foreign financial institutions on qualifying external trade finance lines: 15% under Article 408 E.T. if the lender is a recognized foreign financial entity and the loan is registered with the Central Bank; other cross-border interest and royalty payments to non-domiciled parties: 33% general rate. Treaty-reduced rates typically range from 0-10% for interest and 10% for royalties, subject to TRC submission and beneficial-ownership validation. For a dairy commodity trader, royalty exposure is minimal; parent-company debt must be priced at arm's length and structured within the 3:1 debt-to-equity safe harbor to preserve deductibility.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation, plus the annual transfer-pricing informative return (Form 120), applies where gross income exceeds 135,000 UVT (COP 6,353,775,000 for tax year 2024; UVT = COP 47,065), or where cross-border related-party transactions exist and gross income exceeds 100,000 UVT. Even below these thresholds, the S.A.S. must maintain arm's length support for, inter alia, raw-milk-powder purchases from foreign affiliated suppliers, interest on shareholder loans, commissions and logistics fees.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations regime to ordinary trading S.A.S. entities. However, the DIAN applies substance-over-form principles under Article 5 E.T., the general anti-abuse rule of Article 869 E.T., and the controlled-foreign-corporation rules of Article 882 E.T. A Colombian S.A.S. interposed in the milk-powder trade with no employees, no physical office, no local warehousing, and no commercial decision-making is at risk of being recharacterized as a shell conduit, with transactions re-sourced to the non-resident principals and the 5% dividend surcharge disregarded in favor of full Colombian taxation of the underlying trade income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally suppressing raw-milk-powder trade revenues, inflating costs with false or ghost invoices (falsas facturas), under-declaring customs values, or fabricating freight and storage deductions to reduce the Colombian income tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 402 of the Colombian Criminal Code (Ley 599/2000): imprisonment of 48 to 108 months where the evaded tax exceeds 2,500 monthly minimum wages (COP 3,250,000,000 for 2024; SMLV = COP 1,300,000), plus a fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax and forfeiture of assets used in the fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who endorse or file the fraudulent return face criminal imprisonment, joint and several civil restitution of principal, interest and the 100% inaccuracy penalty, freezing of personal assets, and a DIAN-ordered travel ban (prohibition on leaving Colombian territory) pending criminal and administrative proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False or Late Tax Filing / Inaccuracy (Inexactitud)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting Form 210 with false, incomplete or inconsistent information; failing to file the transfer-pricing informative return Form 120; omitting related-party transactions with the foreign parent or affiliated dairy suppliers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 647 E.T. imposes an inaccuracy penalty of 100% of the greater amount of tax omitted; Article 641 E.T. imposes 5% per month late-filing penalty up to 100% of tax due with a minimum floor of 10 UVT or 0.5% of gross income; monthly default interest accrues on every unpaid peso from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and the certified public accountant (revisor fiscal, where required) are jointly liable for penalties when the declaration is signed without substantive verification. The sanction is not dischargeable in bankruptcy and may trigger involuntary dissolution of the S.A.S. and director ineligibility.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Entity / Piercing the Corporate Veil of the S.A.S.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Colombian S.A.S. as a hollow conduit without employees, premises, inventory risk, or commercial substance, interposed solely to route raw-milk-powder margins to non-resident affiliates and exploit the reduced 5% dividend withholding on taxed profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 42 of Law 1258/2008 (S.A.S. regime) allows Colombian courts to disregard the separate legal personality where the company is used as an instrument of fraud, tax evasion or injury to third parties; the DIAN may recharacterize the transactions under Article 869 E.T. (general anti-abuse rule) and reassess the tax at the 35% corporate rate plus the 100% inaccuracy penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Shareholders and directors become personally liable for the full corporate tax debt, civil restitution, interest and sanctions; personal assets may be attached; directors face prohibitions on managing companies in Colombia and referral to criminal authorities for fraudulent misuse of the corporate vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade-Based Money Laundering and Customs Fraud (Contrabando)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating international trade documentation for whole and skimmed milk powder: inflated or deflated invoices, forged bills of lading, false letters of credit, under-invoicing export cargo, or double-use of customs declarations to shift value out of Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 1762/2015 (anti-smuggling framework) and Article 323 of the Criminal Code (money laundering): imprisonment of 10 to 30 years and fines up to 1,000 SMLV; administrative customs sanctions include seizure and forfeiture of the milk-powder cargo, cancellation of the importer/exporter license, and disqualification from foreign-trade operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign, instruct or benefit from false trade documentation face criminal imprisonment, personal asset forfeiture (extinción de dominio), travel prohibitions, and permanent debarment from Colombian customs brokerage and cross-border trading roles.
